My roommate and I installed a smart thermostat last year, both excited about controlling the temperature from our phones instead of getting up to adjust an actual dial on the wall.
It felt like a genuinely modern upgrade at the time.
What we didn't fully consider was that we have wildly different opinions about temperature.
Now, instead of just adjusting a dial, we each had a convenient app for silently sabotaging the other's preferences.
I'd set it to a comfortable temperature before heading to work.
By the time I got home, it had somehow, mysteriously, dropped several degrees colder, with absolutely no explanation from my roommate about why.
I stood in the hallway for a second, coat still on, genuinely confused about why my own apartment suddenly felt like it belonged somewhere much further north than where we actually lived.
I bumped it back up, said nothing, and went about my evening.
I woke up the next morning to a temperature so cold I could practically see my own breath in the kitchen.
This went on for almost a week.
Neither of us actually addressed it directly, and we just quietly adjusted the app throughout the day, like some kind of slow-motion thermostat standoff between two grown adults.
Eventually, I checked the thermostat's app history, mostly out of curiosity, and discovered an actual log of every single adjustment, complete with timestamps.
It was essentially a detailed record of our entire unspoken thermostat war.
Scrolling through it, I could practically map out both our daily schedules just from the temperature changes alone.
It was a strange, slightly ridiculous timeline of two roommates quietly fighting over a few degrees for an entire week.
I screenshotted the whole ridiculous log and sent it to our group chat.
My roommate immediately replied with a laughing emoji, admitting she'd absolutely been doing it on purpose the whole time.
We actually sat down and talked about it properly.
We landed on a compromise temperature neither of us loved but both could live with, negotiated entirely over takeout on the living room floor.
Honestly, it felt like a small diplomatic victory for our apartment.
Now, whenever one of us touches the thermostat app without asking, the other one just sends a single message, "we had a deal." Somehow, that's been enough to keep the peace ever since.

We even joke about framing that screenshot of the adjustment log someday, hanging it in the hallway as a permanent reminder of the week our apartment briefly became a battlefield over a few measly degrees.
